clue.text: Robots requiring gold to make all transistors and leads

parts.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold
taken as written

indicators.note: the leads of a group of words are the letters at their fronts, so only initials are taken from the run of words

parts.note: the first letters of make, all, transistors and and

explanation.surface: An electronics hobbyist notes that building robots takes gold contacts plus a pile of transistors and wire leads.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leads' looks like electrical wires alongside transistors, but it picks the initial letters of the four words before it.
explanation.definitionFit: Automata are self-operating machines, the older word for mechanical figures that move by themselves like robots.

clue.text: 70s Jagger's sexually ambiguous rock sound

parts.note: short for bisexual

indicators.note: sound tells us to take the noise of a word rather than its spelling, here something heard when spoken

parts.note: a rock is something that holds you steady, an anchor; said in a British accent it ends in an unstressed -uh

explanation.surface: A music writer describes the androgynous 1970s rock sound of Mick Jagger.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface points at Mick, but the 70s Jagger meant is his then wife. Non-rhotic British speech drops the final r of anchor.
explanation.definitionFit: Bianca Jagger was married to Mick Jagger of the Rolling Stones from 1971 until their divorce in 1979.

clue.text: Empty calabash, excellent for tea

indicators.note: an emptied word has lost all its inside letters, leaving only the outer pair

parts.note: the first and last letters of calabash
A1 means excellent; the digit 1 stands in for the letter I

explanation.surface: A hollowed-out gourd turns out to be a fine vessel for brewing tea.
explanation.definitionFit: Chai is the Hindi and widely used word for tea, especially spiced milky tea.

clue.text: Horse turf tipped to be ready

indicators.note: something tipped over is turned end to end, so the pair of words before it is read backwards

parts.note: horse is slang for heroin, abbreviated H
a sod is a piece of turf

explanation.surface: A punter's horse is tipped to win on the turf and be ready for the race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tipped' looks like a racing tip but turns the horse and turf around together. Ready (or readies) is British slang for cash.
explanation.definitionFit: Dosh and ready are both informal British words for money in the hand.

clue.text: Rambling hikes along one of our national symbols?

indicators.note: rambling means wandering about aimlessly, so the letters wander out of their order

parts.note: the ten letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Walkers on a rambling hike pass one of the emblems of the nation.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the tree is an example of a national symbol rather than a synonym. 'Our' is the setter speaking as a Briton.
explanation.definitionFit: The oak tree is a traditional emblem of England, appearing on coins and in Heart of Oak.

clue.text: Tarot card ladies who meet by thorium gaslight?

parts.note: The Fool is a card of the tarot's major arcana
the WI, the Women's Institute, is a British association of women who meet locally
Th is the chemical symbol for thorium, placed next to the previous piece

explanation.surface: A séance scene: tarot cards, a group of women gathering by flickering gaslight.
explanation.walkthrough: Gaslight reads as old-fashioned lamps, but the question mark marks it as the verb meaning to manipulate someone's mind.
explanation.definitionFit: To gaslight is to toy with a person's grip on reality, a cruel kind of messing with and deceiving them.

clue.text: Ugly exfoliating skin rash problem caused by bug?

indicators.note: exfoliating removes the outer layer of skin, so the preceding word sheds its outside letters

parts.note: ugly with its outer letters removed
the itch is an old name for an itching skin rash

explanation.surface: An unsightly peeling rash, perhaps caused by an insect bite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bug' suggests an insect or germ behind the rash; the question mark points to a software bug instead.
explanation.definitionFit: A glitch is a minor malfunction, the sort of fault a programming error produces in a system.

clue.text: ULEZ boundaries backed by prosperous financial centre

indicators.note: backed means moved backwards, so the kept pair is read in the opposite order
the boundaries of a word are its edges, so only its first and last letters are kept

parts.note: the outer letters of ULEZ, London's Ultra Low Emission Zone
prosperous means wealthy

explanation.surface: The edges of London's clean-air zone are said to be funded by a wealthy banking city.
explanation.walkthrough: The ULEZ is the Ultra Low Emission Zone, a charging zone for polluting vehicles in London.
explanation.definitionFit: Zurich is Switzerland's banking capital, home to major banks and a leading stock exchange.

clue.text: Admit Galatians includes old, embarrassing mistake

parts.note: to own up is to admit

indicators.note: includes means takes inside, so one piece is placed within the book's abbreviation

parts.note: Gal is the standard abbreviation for the Epistle to the Galatians
O is the abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: Someone concedes that an old reading of Paul's letter to the Galatians was an embarrassing slip.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally a football goal scored against your own side; figuratively any blunder that harms yourself.

clue.text: Fairly inexperienced solver, no good, is hopeless to begin with

parts.note: the setter addresses the solver as you
NG is the abbreviation for no good
taken as written

indicators.note: to begin with points to the start of the preceding word, so only its opening letter is used

parts.note: the first letter of hopeless

explanation.surface: A fairly green crossword solver is told they are no good and hopeless from the start.
explanation.definitionFit: Youngish means somewhat young, and youth implies limited experience, so fairly inexperienced fits.

clue.text: Devil-woman wantonly hit on one in fifties

indicators.note: wantonly means in an unruly and unrestrained way, so the letters of the short verb break their order
on means placed after, so the rearranged verb is sent second, behind the one-in-fifties piece
in places the single digit within the doubled Roman numeral for fifty

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty; two of them make fifties
I is the Roman numeral for one
the letters of hit rearranged

explanation.surface: A she-devil wantonly strikes at someone in their fifties.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay reads back to front: the rearranged verb goes on, that is after, the one-in-fifties piece.
explanation.definitionFit: In Jewish folklore Lilith is a female demon, said to be Adam's first wife who became a night spirit.

clue.text: Khan's stately home — by a non-Tamil state of India

indicators.note: non- negates the following word, so that word is left out of the state's name

parts.note: X is the multiplication sign, read as by, as in three by four
taken as written
the state of Tamil Nadu without Tamil

explanation.surface: A grand Indian residence is described as lying beside a state other than Tamil Nadu.
explanation.walkthrough: Coleridge's Kubla Khan opens: In Xanadu did Kubla Khan a stately pleasure-dome decree.
explanation.definitionFit: Xanadu was the summer capital of the Mongol emperor Kublai Khan, made famous by Coleridge's poem.

clue.text: Foreign fabricator follows fellow feeding a French friend

indicators.note: follows means comes after, so the fabricator goes at the end
feeding means going into, so one piece is put inside the French phrase

parts.note: un ami is French for a friend
F is the abbreviation for fellow
a fabricator makes things up

explanation.surface: An alliterative tale of a liar trailing a man who keeps feeding a friend from France.
explanation.definitionFit: Foreign can mean strange or not known to someone, as in a concept foreign to them.

clue.text: Italian scorer scores pig hides in the middle

indicators.note: in the middle tells us the letters sit inside the run of words, not at their edges

parts.note: running across the end of scores, all of pig and the start of hides

explanation.surface: A gourmet scores pig hides, the pork rind, somewhere in the middle of a dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scorer' sounds like a goal scorer, but it is someone who writes musical scores.
explanation.definitionFit: Ottorino Respighi was an Italian composer, best known for the Pines of Rome and Fountains of Rome.

clue.text: Got to retire delirious once free from obligations

indicators.note: to retire is to draw back, so the remaining letters run backwards
once free from means after being released from something, so those letters are dropped from the word

parts.note: taken as written
IOUs are written promises to pay, so they are obligations; these letters are removed

explanation.surface: A worker eager to retire becomes giddy with relief once out of debt.
explanation.walkthrough: Delirious happens to end in the letters of the debt notes, so removing them leaves a five-letter stub to turn round.
explanation.definitionFit: To get to someone is an idiom for annoying them, and riled is the past tense meaning irritated.

clue.text: Foretell of conflicts undergoing polar shift

indicators.note: a polar shift swaps one pole for the other, so a south abbreviation becomes a north one

parts.note: conflicts are wars

explanation.surface: A prophet foretells wars as the Earth's magnetic poles flip.
explanation.walkthrough: S for south becomes N for north.
explanation.definitionFit: To warn is to give advance notice of danger, telling of something before it happens.

clue.text: Nervous society filled with tense people unable to take sides

indicators.note: filled with means having something put inside, so the grammar letter goes within

parts.note: neural means relating to the nerves
S is the abbreviation for society
T is the grammar abbreviation for tense

explanation.surface: A nervous, tense group of people cannot bring themselves to pick a side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nervous' and 'tense' both look like moods, but one is the adjective for the nervous system and the other a grammar abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Neutrals are people or countries that stay out of a dispute without supporting either party.

clue.text: Folded in half then turned back sides of origami paper

indicators.note: in half means only half of the word is kept, here its front three letters

parts.note: the first half of folded

indicators.note: turned back means facing the other way, so the two side letters swap order
the sides of a word are its first and last letters

parts.note: the first and last letters of origami

explanation.surface: Origami instructions: fold the sheet in half, then turn back its edges.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as folding paper; in fact 'Folded' and 'origami' are each cut down to a few letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A folio is a sheet of paper folded once, or a single leaf of a book or manuscript.

clue.text: Holiday job initially involves a day trip to Saudi

indicators.note: involves means wraps around, so the two letters that follow go inside
initially points to the opening letters of the two words before it

parts.note: the first letters of holiday and job
taken as written
D is the abbreviation for day

explanation.surface: A holiday job comes with a day trip to Saudi Arabia.
explanation.definitionFit: The hadj or hajj is the Muslim pilgrimage to Mecca, in Saudi Arabia, a duty once in a lifetime.

clue.text: Full range of notes expressed in sad piano movement

indicators.note: a movement shifts things about, so the letters are moved into a new order

parts.note: the eight letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A melancholy piano movement explores every note of the scale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Movement' looks like part of a sonata, but it signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: A diapason is the entire compass of musical tones, an instrument or voice's complete range.

clue.text: Used Hoover Dam upper curve whilst overlooking river meanders

indicators.note: overlooking means ignoring, so the river abbreviation is left out of the curve
meanders means wanders along a winding course, so the letters wind into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
U is the abbreviation for upper-class
curve with R, the river, overlooked

explanation.surface: A view of the Hoover Dam's upper curve above a meandering river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hoover' looks like the dam's name, but used as a verb it is the British word for vacuum cleaning.
explanation.definitionFit: Hoover is a brand of cleaner that became the British verb for vacuum cleaning a floor or carpet.

clue.text: Nearly a thousand missing outside

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: outside means one piece wraps around another, so the word for missing goes round the thousand

parts.note: missing means lost
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand

explanation.surface: Close to a thousand people are reported missing.
explanation.definitionFit: Almost and nearly are synonyms meaning not quite, very close to a given amount.

clue.text: Grizzly relative I knocked out first with attack on both sides

indicators.note: first says the knocked-out piece leads, coming ahead of the single letter rather than after it

parts.note: KO'd means knocked out, placed first as the clue says
taken as written

indicators.note: both sides of a word are its two ends, so its first and last letters are kept

parts.note: the first and last letters of attack

explanation.surface: Someone boasts of being first to knock out a grizzly bear's cousin as it attacked from both sides.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I knocked out first' means the knocked-out piece comes before I, not I first.
explanation.definitionFit: The Kodiak is a large brown bear of Alaska, a subspecies closely related to the grizzly.

clue.text: Fats make protein-building acid non-active

indicators.note: non-active means without active, whose abbreviation is dropped from the acid

parts.note: to do is to make, as in do a drawing
amino acids build proteins; amino with A, for active, removed

explanation.surface: A nutrition note: fats help make protein-building amino acids inactive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fats' poses as dietary fat in a biochemistry surface, but it names a musician.
explanation.definitionFit: Fats Domino was the stage name of Antoine Domino, the New Orleans rock and roll pianist and singer.

clue.text: Doctor thrown into Russian river under cover of darkness

indicators.note: thrown into means placed inside, so the doctor goes within the river's name

parts.note: the Ural is a river flowing from the Russian Urals to the Caspian
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's degree

explanation.surface: A doctor is dumped into a Russian river at night.
explanation.definitionFit: Umbral is an adjective for shadow, from Latin umbra, describing something lying in shade or darkness.

clue.text: Measure what one eats a bit at a time

parts.note: an inch is a measure of length
a meal is what one eats

explanation.surface: Advice to measure out your food and eat it in small portions.
explanation.definitionFit: Inchmeal is an old adverb meaning gradually, by small degrees, an inch at a time.

clue.text: One country's nationalist going to question another

parts.note: the IRA, the Irish Republican Army, was a nationalist paramilitary group
Q is the abbreviation for question

explanation.surface: A patriot from one nation sets off to interrogate a rival nation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Another' carries on from 'one country', so it defines a second country.
explanation.definitionFit: Iraq is a Middle Eastern nation, so it stands as a further instance of a country.

clue.text: Complain about BBC English

parts.note: ca, short for circa, means about
RP, Received Pronunciation, is the standard accent once heard on the BBC

explanation.surface: A listener moans about the posh accent of BBC announcers.
explanation.definitionFit: To carp is to find fault and grumble persistently about trivial matters.

clue.text: Somewhat insult an Arab ruler's wife

indicators.note: somewhat means a part of, so only a stretch of the words that follow is used

parts.note: spanning the end of insult, all of an and the start of Arab

explanation.surface: A mild insult aimed at the wife of an Arab ruler.
explanation.definitionFit: A sultana is the wife or consort of a sultan, the sovereign of a Muslim state.

clue.text: Two characters making the case for Romeo having married by chance

parts.note: the two letters spelt out as one letter and another

indicators.note: a case is an outer casing, so the two characters wanted are the edges of the name

parts.note: the outer letters of Romeo, written out as R and O
M is the abbreviation for married

explanation.surface: A lawyer presents the case for Romeo having secretly married.
explanation.walkthrough: The joining word between the two edge letters is spelt out and becomes part of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Random describes something happening without plan or pattern, purely by chance.
